reference.sentence: The company decided to invest in new technology, and ___ has already led to a 20% rise in productivity.
reference.explanation: This retoma la idea entera de la frase anterior (la decisión de invertir).

reference.sentence: 'The train's been cancelled again.' '___'s ridiculous!'
reference.explanation: That para reaccionar a lo que ha dicho otra persona.

reference.sentence: She's been working here for ten years — ___ 's why she knows everything.
reference.explanation: That's why... para dar razones.

reference.sentence: Several economists were consulted. ___ economists agreed that a recession was unlikely.
reference.explanation: These + sustantivo retoma algo ya mencionado.

reference.sentence: ___ who studied regularly passed the exam easily.
reference.explanation: Those who = las personas que (en general).

reference.sentence: Our prices are lower than ___ of our competitors.
reference.explanation: Those of + sustantivo para no repetir 'prices'.

reference.sentence: We could build a park or a car park. The ___ would benefit families, while the latter would only help drivers.
reference.explanation: The former = el primero de dos.

reference.sentence: Tom and Jack applied for the job. The ___ got it because he had more experience — Tom was really disappointed.
reference.explanation: The latter = el segundo de dos (Jack).

reference.sentence: He shouted at the referee and threw his boots. ___ behaviour is completely unacceptable.
reference.explanation: Such + sustantivo = un comportamiento así.

reference.sentence: I'd never heard of ___ a thing before.
reference.explanation: Such a + sustantivo.

reference.sentence: She ordered the grilled fish, and I had ___.
reference.explanation: The same = lo mismo.

reference.sentence: He refused to apologise, ___ made the situation even worse.
reference.explanation: Which (con coma) retoma toda la oración anterior.

reference.sentence: Artists now have a vast range of materials. ___ means that they can be much more versatile than in the past.
reference.explanation: This / that / it retoman la frase anterior.

reference.sentence: There are two candidates. I prefer the one with experience; the ___ seems a bit too young.
reference.explanation: The other = el segundo de dos.

reference.sentence: I invited all my classmates, but only a few came. The ___ said they were busy.
reference.explanation: The others = el resto.

reference.sentence: Correct it: When things like ___ happen, it's better to just relax. (the trains were cancelled)
reference.explanation: Things like that / this: retoma la situación mencionada (✗ things like these).

reference.sentence: Correct it: She is a baker who produces excellent cakes. And ___ is what matters. (2 words → 1 word)
reference.explanation: That (singular) retoma toda la idea (✗ those are what matters).

reference.sentence: Hundreds of people want to go to Mars, but only a small number ___ will be accepted.
reference.explanation: Of them evita repetir 'people'.

reference.sentence: My grandparents were born in Italy. ___ is where my love of pasta comes from.
reference.explanation: That is where / that's why... retoma la idea.

reference.sentence: Many people complained about the noise, ___ was hardly surprising.
reference.explanation: Which retoma la oración entera (relativo con coma).

substitution.sentence: I really enjoyed the books you lent me, especially the ___ about ancient history.
substitution.explanation: Ones sustituye al plural 'books'.

substitution.sentence: Mary didn't finish the assignment on time, but I ___.
substitution.explanation: Auxiliar del past simple en lugar de repetir 'finished'.

substitution.sentence: He asked if the train was delayed and I told him I hoped ___.
substitution.explanation: Hope + not = espero que no.

substitution.sentence: 'Are you going to the concert?' 'I'm not sure. If ___, we could share a taxi.'
substitution.explanation: If so = si es así.

substitution.sentence: We need to submit the report by Friday. If ___, we'll lose the contract.
substitution.explanation: If not = si no es así.

substitution.sentence: I don't think we should buy a new car, and neither ___ my wife.
substitution.explanation: Neither + aux + sujeto (does por 'my wife', present simple).

substitution.sentence: I really enjoy science fiction novels. So ___ my best friend.
substitution.explanation: So + aux + sujeto.

substitution.sentence: 'You've got paint on your shirt!' 'Oh, so I ___!'
substitution.explanation: So I have! = confirmación sorprendida (orden sujeto + aux).

substitution.sentence: They promised to clean the house before we arrived, and they duly ___ so.
substitution.explanation: Do so = verbo + complementos (formal).

substitution.sentence: I used to play tennis a lot, but I haven't ___ so for years.
substitution.explanation: Present perfect de do so: have done so.

substitution.sentence: She was wearing a beautiful dress, the ___ I bought for her birthday.
substitution.explanation: One = 'the dress' (contable singular).

substitution.sentence: 'Will the new policy affect our department?' 'Don't worry — I don't think ___.'
substitution.explanation: I don't think so (la negación va en think).

substitution.sentence: 'Will it rain during the wedding?' 'I hope ___.'
substitution.explanation: I hope not (✗ I don't hope so).

substitution.sentence: 'Can you lend me £50?' 'I'm afraid ___.'
substitution.explanation: I'm afraid not = me temo que no.

substitution.sentence: My old phone was broken, so I had to buy a new ___.
substitution.explanation: A + adj + one.

substitution.sentence: There are two jackets. You can take ___ — I don't mind which.
substitution.explanation: Either = cualquiera de los dos.

substitution.sentence: He's written two novels and ___ has been translated into English.
substitution.explanation: Neither (de dos) + verbo singular.

substitution.sentence: Correct it: Having broken mine, I needed a new camera, so I was delighted when my partner gave me ___ as a present.
substitution.explanation: One = una cámara cualquiera (✗ it = esa cámara concreta).

substitution.sentence: 'Is Sophie meeting us there?' 'I think ___.'
substitution.explanation: Think + so sustituye la oración afirmativa.

substitution.sentence: My children won't eat green apples. Do you have any red ___?
substitution.explanation: Ones sustituye 'apples'.

ellipsis.sentence: I have never been scuba diving, but my brother ___.
She promised to help me, but in the end she didn't want ___.
The manager resigned suddenly, and nobody understands ___.
I thought the meeting was going to be cancelled, but it ___.
'Would you like to come to the cinema?' 'I'd love ___!'
Someone left the door open, but I don't know ___.
ellipsis.explanation: Who = el sujeto que falta (who left it open).

ellipsis.sentence: I didn't go to the party, but I could ___.
'Has the parcel been sent yet?' 'It should ___ by now.'
ellipsis.explanation: Ellipsis tras modal perfect pasivo (should have been sent).

ellipsis.sentence: I don't smoke now, but I ___ to.
Give me a call later if you're able ___.
I'd like to solve your problem, but I'm not sure I'd be allowed ___.
Which of these sentences correctly omits the relative pronoun?
options: The car I bought is very fast.
The man called you is my boss.
The book is on the table is mine.
The girl won the prize is my sister.
ellipsis.answer: The car I bought is very fast.
ellipsis.explanation: Solo se omite si el relativo es objeto (detrás hay un sujeto: I).

ellipsis.sentence: Which sentence uses ellipsis correctly?
options: She can sing but can't dance.
She can sing but she can't.
She can sing but can't to dance.
She can sing but dance can't.
ellipsis.answer: She can sing but can't dance.
ellipsis.explanation: Se omite el sujeto repetido tras but.

ellipsis.sentence: 'Have you finished your essay?' 'Not yet, but I ___ by tonight.'
Kim suggested going to the ballet, but I didn't want ___.
'Sounds good to me.' What has been omitted?
We used to go to the cinema every weekend, but we haven't ___ recently.
Most of the class are walking to college now. You should ___. (1 word: también)
A year ago I couldn't drive a car, but now I ___.
'We only have vanilla or chocolate.' 'That's fine. ___ will be OK.'

book.sentence: There are only a few slices of cake left. Take ___ while you've got the chance.
Because of the snow, all the trains were cancelled. I realised that when things like ___ happen, it's better to just relax.
book.explanation: Book ex.1: ✗ things like these → ✓ things like that.

book.sentence: She exhibited some wonderful photos, the best of ___ was taken in South Africa.
book.explanation: Book ex.1: ✗ the best of these → ✓ the best of which.

book.sentence: The best candidates are ___ that show they have done their homework.
The fans were chanting for Simons, the man in ___ ability the crowd always put their faith.
She knows how to produce excellent cakes. And ___ is what matters.
book.explanation: Book ex.1: ✗ those are → ✓ that is.

book.sentence: I needed a new camera, so I was delighted when my partner gave me ___ as a present.
It was clearly a dangerous journey, and everyone had told her ___.
book.explanation: Book ex.2: told her so = told her it would be dangerous.

book.sentence: We used to go to the cinema every weekend, but we haven't ___ recently.
book.explanation: Book ex.2: haven't been (to the cinema).

book.sentence: Most of the class are walking to college now. You should ___ too.
book.explanation: Book ex.2: you should too / you should do so.
